answer: Each identity carries a hash chain anchored by a beacon. Each epoch the beacon publishes a seed, and a chain extends only with a comet link hashing the previous answer with that seed. Key-bound links cannot be copied or merged. A new identity posts a 40-credit bond; a broken link or missed epoch burns it and resets standing to zero. The k-th fake still needs its own bond and chain, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits. A rented-chain ring fails because a borrowed link mismatches its key. A raven auditor recomputes each comet link and forfeits a forged bond. Honest identities pay one bond.
